key_idea: Evaluating a topological intersection form on polynomial-weighted cycles yields a non-degenerate bilinear form whose isotropic subspace dimension forces a strict lower bound on the crossing number.
reason: This proof completely bypasses the notoriously heavy combinatorial case analysis of crossing numbers by translating the problem into algebra. By cleanly exploiting the intersection form of planar cycles and Lagrange interpolation, it derives a massive combinatorial result from wonderfully minimal algebraic machinery.
